text: Kìraitū Mūrungi (born 1 January 1952) is a Kenyan politician, lawyer, and civil rights advocate who currently serves as the Chairman of the National Oil Corporation of Kenya, a position he was appointed to in 2023. He was born in Kionyo Village, Meru District, and attended Kionyo Primary School, Chuka High School, and Alliance High School. He earned a Bachelor of Laws from the University of Nairobi in 1977 and later an LLM from the same university in 1982. In 1991, he completed a second LLM at Harvard Law School while in exile in the United States. Before entering politics, he was a partner in a law firm co-founded with Gibson Kamau Kuria and Aaron Ringera, where he represented political prisoners during Daniel arap Moi's presidency, including Wanyiri Kihoro, and advocated for human rights and social justice. He joined the Forum for the Restoration of Democracy (FORD) and later the Democratic Party (DP) to promote multi-party democracy. Mūrungi was elected Member of Parliament for South Imenti in 1992 and held the seat until 2013, aligning with reformist leaders and joining the National Rainbow Coalition (NARC) in 2002. He served in various cabinet roles, including Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs and Minister of Energy. In 2013, he became Senator for Meru County and in 2017, he was elected Governor of Meru County under the Jubilee Party, serving a five-year term. His political career has been marked by controversies: in 2005, he faced criticism for a remark perceived as trivializing corruption and gender violence, for which he apologized; he was also implicated in the Anglo Leasing Scandal, with recordings released in 2006 by John Githongo alleging he attempted to obstruct investigations, though he denied the claims and resigned from his cabinet post to allow further inquiry, later returning as Minister of Energy. Mūrungi is married to Priscilla Mūrungi and has four children. He is recognized as a visionary leader and social organizer who has significantly contributed to the development of South Imenti Constituency and has had a profound influence on Kenyan politics and governance, particularly through his advocacy for democratic reforms.
